content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Built a complete bookmark manager called **Nest**.

Features include:

- Add, edit, delete, and favorite bookmarks
- Search with `⌘/Ctrl + K`
- Collections and recent/favorite filters
- Grid and list views
- Sorting by date or title
- Local browser persistence
- Responsive mobile navigation
- Polished empty states and notifications

Verified with a production build, Playwright workflow tests, and responsive checks at mobile, tablet, and desktop widths.

Open the app at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000).

This is looking really polished — I like how calm and clean it feels, and I can see it already handles adding, editing, favoriting, searching, collections, and sorting. Nice work.

Two things are holding me back from calling it done, though:

1. When I go to add a bookmark, it looks like I have to type in the title and description myself, and the little colored squares are just initials rather than the actual site icons. What I really pictured is: I paste in a link, and the app goes and fetches the page's title, description, and icon for me automatically so I barely have to type anything. That "just paste the link" convenience is honestly the main reason I wanted this — right now saving a link feels like filling out a form.

2. A big part of why I save links is to come back and read them later. I'd like to be able to mark a bookmark as "to read," and then see just those unread ones on their own, and check them off once I've read them.

Could you get those working? The rest of what you showed is close to what I had in mind.

content:
Implemented both additions.

- Paste a URL and Nest automatically fetches its title, description, final URL, and favicon.
- Fields remain editable when metadata is incomplete or unavailable.
- New bookmarks default to “To read.”
- Added a dedicated reading queue with live counts.
- Bookmarks can be marked read or returned to the queue in one click.
- Existing saved data migrates safely to the new format.

Verified against a real page from web.dev, plus four passing Playwright tests covering metadata autofill, saving, filtering, and marking items read.

Review it at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000).

This is exactly what I was hoping for. Pasting a link now pulls in the title, description, and the real site icon on its own, and I can still fix anything it doesn't get — that's the effortless saving I wanted. And the "To read" queue with the count, plus being able to mark something read or drop it back in the queue in one click, is just how I pictured managing my reading.

Both of the things I raised are handled, and everything else you'd shown was already what I had in mind. I'm happy with this — it does what I set out to build.
